paragraphs: Differential equations offer a way to understand optimization by treating an algorithm as a continuous process. A Lyapunov functional tracks progress and can reveal how quickly that process approaches a solution. The difficulty is translating this continuous analysis into an algorithm that takes discrete steps: existing approaches often require a separate convergence argument for each method.

The paper introduces a weak discrete gradient, a mathematical concept that collects the conditions needed for discrete gradient expressions to support these arguments. Using this concept, the authors define abstract optimization methods and establish convergence theories that mirror their continuous counterparts. This makes the passage from differential equations to implementable updates more systematic.

Many familiar optimization algorithms and their convergence rates emerge as special cases of the framework. Its contribution is therefore both organizational and constructive: it brings existing analyses under one theory and provides a setting for developing new methods. Within convex optimization, the authors describe competitive convergence rates relative to methods such as Nesterov’s accelerated gradient.
neurips-2023-a-unified-discretization-fr.tldr: A weak discrete gradient framework systematically translates continuous differential-equation analyses into discrete convex optimization methods and convergence guarantees.

paragraphs: Adaptive step sizes can make stochastic gradient descent effective for overparameterized models, but their guarantees become less satisfactory outside interpolation settings. Existing stochastic Polyak step sizes and line searches may converge only to a neighborhood of a solution. Artificially shrinking the steps can address this issue while sacrificing convergence speed under interpolation.

The paper introduces AdaSPS and AdaSLS to improve this tradeoff. Their asymptotic rates are optimal across the stated convexity and interpolation settings, with an explicit exception when strong convexity and non-interpolation occur together. AdaSLS needs no problem-dependent parameters, while AdaSPS requires a lower bound on the optimal objective value. These input requirements matter for making adaptive updates usable without extensive problem-specific information.

The authors also develop a variance-reduction method that supports acceleration with either Polyak step sizes or line search. Combined with the proposed adaptive variants, it obtains the optimal rate for smooth convex objectives. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support the theoretical analysis and the methods’ reported effectiveness and robustness.
neurips-2023-adaptive-sgd-with-polyak-st.tldr: AdaSPS and AdaSLS improve adaptive SGD guarantees across several settings and support a new variance-reduction approach with accelerated convergence.

paragraphs: Brant is a pretrained model for intracranial recordings, designed to provide reusable representations of neural signals. The authors train it on a large collection of intracranial data they gathered and describe it as the largest model in the brain-signal field. The central aim is to make one pretrained model useful across multiple subsequent tasks.

Its design combines information from the time and frequency domains while capturing long-term temporal dependencies and spatial correlations. These perspectives address different aspects of the same recordings: how signals develop over time, how their frequency content behaves, and how signals relate across locations. Bringing them together supports a representation that can serve more than one prediction problem.

The authors report state-of-the-art results for neural-signal forecasting, frequency-phase forecasting, imputation, and seizure detection. Analyses with limited labels and visualizations of the learned representations further support their pretraining strategy. Their model-size investigation also finds that greater capacity can improve performance on their dataset, providing dataset-specific evidence for scaling the approach.
neurips-2023-brant-foundation-model-for-.tldr: Brant combines temporal, spatial, and frequency information in a pretrained intracranial-signal model that performs strongly across several downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Editing an image through text can accidentally alter its background or other objects, particularly when those objects resemble or relate to the intended target. The authors’ experiments identify inaccurate cross-attention maps as the source of this problem. These maps connect parts of the text prompt with image regions, so incorrect associations can spread an edit beyond its intended area.

Dynamic Prompt Learning addresses this leakage by updating the representations of noun tokens in the prompt. Its repair losses guide cross-attention toward the correct noun-object associations. Built on Stable Diffusion, the approach aims to make edits more selective by improving the internal connection between the named object and the region being changed.

Across a wide range of evaluated images, the authors report consistently stronger quantitative results using CLIP score and Structure-Dist, alongside favorable user evaluations. Improvements cover word replacement, prompt refinement, and attention reweighting, with particular benefits in complex scenes containing multiple objects. The findings support targeted attention repair as a useful mechanism for finer editing control.
neurips-2023-dynamic-prompt-learning-add.tldr: Dynamic Prompt Learning updates noun representations to repair cross-attention leakage and make text-driven image edits more selective.

paragraphs: EPIC Fields adds 3D camera information to EPIC-KITCHENS so researchers can study geometry and video understanding together. Recovering cameras from video is a difficult and expensive preparatory step, especially in first-person recordings containing dynamic actions. The authors introduce innovations for this reconstruction problem and provide the resulting camera information as part of the dataset.

The resource combines geometry with existing action labels and VISOR segmentation annotations. This pairing makes it useful for questions that involve both how a scene is arranged and what happens within it. The reconstruction covers 96% of EPIC-KITCHENS videos, registering 19 million frames across 99 hours of recordings from 45 kitchens.

The paper also evaluates benchmark tasks in neural rendering and dynamic-object segmentation. Strong baselines expose remaining challenges, giving researchers concrete problems to work on with the new resource. Separately, the authors demonstrate an advantage from geometry in semi-supervised video-object segmentation using VISOR annotations. The contribution therefore includes both reusable reconstruction data and evidence of its relevance to video analysis.
neurips-2023-epic-fields-marrying-3d-geo.tldr: EPIC Fields enriches EPIC-KITCHENS with reconstructed 3D camera information and benchmarks connecting neural rendering with video understanding.

paragraphs: Free-Bloom targets videos whose frames express a meaningful progression, such as the stages of a flower opening. Producing visually plausible movement alone does not establish that progression. The paper separates the task of planning what happens over time from the task of generating the images that depict it.

A large language model acts as the director, turning the requested content into a coherent sequence of prompts. A pretrained latent diffusion model then acts as the animator, producing frames from that sequence. To support continuity of appearance and motion alongside the planned semantics, the authors modify the reverse diffusion process using joint noise sampling, step-aware attention shift, and dual-path interpolation.

The pipeline requires neither video data nor additional training for its video-generation procedure. The authors report high-quality results, including complex scenes with meaningful frame sequences, and describe compatibility with extensions based on latent diffusion models. The approach matters because it combines existing language and image-generation capabilities to address temporal storytelling without introducing a video-training requirement.
neurips-2023-free-bloom-zero-shot-text-t.tldr: Free-Bloom uses a language model to plan evolving scenes and pretrained diffusion models to animate them without video data or additional training.

paragraphs: Tabular learning becomes difficult when a dataset has far more features than labeled examples. With so little evidence relative to the number of inputs, a model can overfit. PLATO addresses this setting by using auxiliary domain knowledge about the features themselves, represented as a heterogeneous knowledge graph.

Each input feature corresponds to a graph node and to a weight vector in the first layer of a multilayer perceptron. PLATO links these two representations through a trainable message-passing function that infers the weight vector from the feature’s graph node. Its guiding assumption is that features represented by similar graph nodes should receive similar first-layer weight vectors.

This mechanism uses relationships among features to regularize the predictive model when labeled samples are scarce. Across six datasets with many more features than samples, the authors report outperforming 13 state-of-the-art baselines, with gains reaching 10.19%. The results support using an available feature knowledge graph to structure model weights in this challenging data regime.
neurips-2023-high-dimensional-tabular-de.tldr: PLATO uses a knowledge graph of input features to regularize neural-network weights for tabular datasets with many features and few samples.

paragraphs: LAMM provides an open research ecosystem for language models that work with visual information as well as text. The authors motivate it through the limited transparency of existing multimodal systems, which makes academic investigation harder. Their contribution combines instruction-tuning data, evaluation benchmarks, and a training framework instead of supplying only a model.

The dataset and benchmark cover a broad range of tasks in both 2D and 3D vision. The paper also explains how to construct multimodal instruction datasets and benchmarks, supporting extension to additional domains, tasks, and modalities. Its initial training framework is specifically designed to accommodate modality expansion, while baseline models and experimental analyses provide starting points for further research.

Experiments support the usefulness of the dataset and benchmark. The reported baseline training uses 24 A100 GPU hours, and the framework also supports training on V100 and RTX3090 hardware. Together, these resources make multimodal instruction-tuning methods more accessible to study and extend, while the broader goal remains enabling richer interaction between people and AI agents.
neurips-2023-lamm-language-assisted-mult.tldr: LAMM supplies open multimodal instruction data, benchmarks, and an extensible training framework spanning 2D and 3D vision tasks.

paragraphs: Rule-based knowledge graph completion uses existing relationships to infer missing ones. Restricting this reasoning to graph structure can leave useful textual evidence unused. This paper introduces a two-stage framework that brings information from a text corpus into the process of learning rules for graph completion.

First, the method extracts candidate triples with confidence scores, called soft triples. A textual entailment model uses multiple sentences to estimate whether they support a proposed relationship, with distant supervision supplying the learning signal. Second, the system uses these soft triples to train a rule-based model. Because text-derived candidates can be noisy, the authors introduce text-enhanced rules designed to reduce their negative effects.

A neural model simulates inference with these rules. The authors prove that any set of text-enhanced rules can be represented by some parameter assignment of that model, establishing a representational guarantee. They also introduce three evaluation datasets and report significant improvements in inductive link prediction from combining soft triples with the proposed rules.
neurips-2023-learning-from-both-structur.tldr: A two-stage framework converts textual evidence into confidence-weighted triples and learns text-enhanced rules for inductive knowledge graph completion.

paragraphs: Learning a dynamic process from observations is difficult when measurements are noisy, incomplete, and scattered irregularly across space and time. This paper introduces a neural partial differential equation model that operates independently of a fixed observation grid. It represents the underlying state continuously in space and time, allowing the model to address partially observed processes.

The approach combines a probabilistic framework with an encoder designed for data efficiency and grid independence. A PDE governs the latent state’s evolution, using a combination of collocation and the method of lines. Amortized variational inference estimates an approximate posterior, while multiple shooting is used to improve training speed and stability.

These components connect uncertain observations with a continuously evolving hidden representation. On complex synthetic and real-world datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art performance and improvements over recent methods, including effective handling of partial observations. The findings support the potential of this formulation for learning dynamic processes when the available measurements do not fit a complete, regular space-time grid.
neurips-2023-learning-space-time-continu.tldr: A continuous latent neural PDE model learns dynamic processes from noisy, partial observations on irregular space-time grids.

paragraphs: Sequential decisions require uncertainty estimates that remain trustworthy as new observations arrive. Standard confidence constructions often depend on specialized arguments for a particular model, noise distribution, and estimator. This paper proposes likelihood-ratio confidence sequences as a more general approach, with validity that holds across observation times.

The method is especially suited to settings with well-specified likelihoods. Its confidence sets maintain the prescribed coverage, while their size depends on the estimator sequence used in the likelihood ratio. The authors investigate principled choices of that sequence and connect the problem to online convex optimization, including Follow-the-Regularized-Leader. This distinguishes the validity of the uncertainty statement from how informative its resulting set is.

A reweighting scheme addresses large initial estimator bias and enables use with nonparametric function classes such as reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The paper also gives finite-sample size analysis for generalized linear models. Applications to generalized linear bandits, survival analysis, and bandits with different additive noise distributions demonstrate the method’s practical range.
neurips-2023-likelihood-ratio-confidence.tldr: Likelihood-ratio confidence sequences provide anytime-valid uncertainty estimates, with estimator selection and reweighting helping control their size.

paragraphs: Meta learning adjusts how a learning system learns, but its computational and memory demands can make large-scale use difficult. Training instability and limited distributed support add further obstacles. SAMA addresses these practical barriers by combining changes to implicit differentiation with systems techniques for efficient training.

The method supports a broad range of adaptive optimizers within the underlying learning process. It avoids explicitly computing second-order gradient information and uses distributed training techniques developed for first-order gradients. On large-scale meta-learning benchmarks, the authors report throughput gains of up to 1.7 times on one GPU and 4.8 times across multiple GPUs, alongside memory reductions of up to 2.0 and 3.8 times respectively.

The paper also examines what this efficiency enables. SAMA-based data optimization consistently improves text-classification accuracy with BERT and RoBERTa, and achieves state-of-the-art results in small- and large-scale image-data pruning. These findings connect the computational improvements to useful language and vision applications, showing that scalable meta learning can support better choices about training data.
neurips-2023-making-scalable-meta-learni.tldr: SAMA combines implicit differentiation and distributed training techniques to reduce meta-learning costs and support effective data optimization.

paragraphs: The k-means++ algorithm is a widely used starting point for clustering, with an expected approximation guarantee that grows logarithmically with the number of clusters. Previous work improved that guarantee by adding local-search steps based on the same sampling distribution, obtaining a constant approximation factor. This paper asks how much stronger such local improvement can become.

The proposed algorithm expands the search neighborhood so that it can replace multiple cluster centers at once. Considering coordinated changes gives the search more sophisticated ways to improve the clustering objective. The authors prove an approximation ratio of 9 plus epsilon and describe this as the best possible guarantee for local search.

The contribution also addresses whether the stronger search can be useful in practice. The authors report that their algorithm is easy to implement, runs fast enough on a variety of classic datasets, and produces solutions with better objective cost. Thus, the paper connects a sharper theoretical guarantee with an implementation that remains practical on the evaluated clustering problems.
neurips-2023-multi-swap-k-means-42fed0df.tldr: Allowing coordinated swaps of multiple centers gives k-means++ local search a 9-plus-epsilon approximation guarantee and better reported clustering costs.

paragraphs: Neural radiance fields generate new views by integrating information along viewing rays. In practice, this integral is evaluated through finitely many samples. The conventional formula corresponds to assuming constant density within successive intervals, and the authors identify an instability: changing the sampling locations can change the rendered result in problematic ways.

The paper replaces that formulation with one corresponding to an exact integral under piecewise linear density. Density can therefore vary linearly within intervals rather than remaining constant. This mathematical change addresses conflicts between samples on different rays, imprecision in hierarchical sampling, and the inability to differentiate certain ray-termination quantiles with respect to model parameters.

The authors demonstrate sharper textures, improved geometric reconstruction, and stronger use of depth supervision compared with the classical rendering equation. They also describe the formulation as a drop-in replacement for existing NeRF-based methods. Its significance is that improvements arise from revisiting the numerical rendering model itself, making the contribution applicable within methods that already rely on volume rendering.
neurips-2023-nerf-revisited-fixing-quadr.tldr: A volume-rendering formula based on piecewise linear density resolves sampling instability and improves reported NeRF texture, geometry, and depth supervision.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks model relationships among entities, but their ability to represent interactions needs a more precise account than general statements about expressive power. This paper studies interactions across a partition of the graph: one group of vertices on one side and all remaining vertices on the other.

The authors quantify interaction strength using separation rank. For the GNNs covered by their analysis, interaction capacity is primarily governed by the partition’s walk index, a graph property based on walks originating at the partition boundary. Experiments with common GNN architectures support this connection. The result links a model’s ability to combine information across groups to a concrete feature of graph structure.

The authors turn the theory into Walk Index Sparsification, an algorithm for removing edges while preserving interaction-modeling capacity. They describe it as simple and computationally efficient, and report markedly better resulting prediction accuracy than alternative sparsification methods in their experiments. This application shows how an analysis of interactions can guide practical decisions about which graph connections to retain.
neurips-2023-on-the-ability-of-graph-neu.tldr: A graph’s walk index helps characterize GNN interaction capacity and guides an effective edge-sparsification algorithm.

paragraphs: In standard online convex optimization, a learner repeatedly chooses an action and incurs a loss associated with that current choice. Many applications have longer consequences: today’s loss depends on the entire sequence of earlier decisions. This paper introduces a framework that represents that history dependence directly, without restricting attention to a fixed memory window.

The central quantity is p-effective memory capacity, denoted H_p, which measures the maximum influence of past decisions on present losses. The authors prove a policy-regret upper bound proportional to the square root of H_p times the number of rounds. A matching worst-case lower bound establishes that the memory dependence cannot generally be improved within the framework.

The analysis also yields the first nontrivial lower bound for the finite-memory setting and improves existing upper bounds there. Applications include online linear control and an online form of performative prediction. For these problems, the framework provides regret guarantees and can simplify or strengthen earlier derivations by treating persistent effects of decisions explicitly.
neurips-2023-online-convex-optimization-.tldr: An online optimization framework captures unlimited decision history through effective memory capacity and establishes matching worst-case regret bounds.

paragraphs: Competitive reinforcement learning must balance learning about the environment with acting effectively against another player. This paper studies posterior sampling in zero-sum Markov games with general function approximation. It considers both self-play, where the learning procedure controls both players, and adversarial learning, where it faces an opponent’s policies.

The authors introduce separate generalized eluder coefficients for these two settings. These complexity measures capture the exploration-exploitation difficulty associated with function approximation. Using the self-play coefficient, they develop a model-based posterior-sampling algorithm for learning a Nash equilibrium that also handles partially observed states. For adversarial learning, they identify suitable partially observable model classes and construct a corresponding sampling method.

The proposed algorithms receive low-regret guarantees that can scale sublinearly with both the relevant coefficient and the number of episodes. The authors present the framework as applicable to a majority of tractable zero-sum Markov-game classes under full or partial observation. Its contribution is a common theoretical treatment of posterior sampling across these distinct competitive-learning situations.
neurips-2023-posterior-sampling-for-comp.tldr: Generalized eluder coefficients support posterior-sampling algorithms and regret guarantees for self-play and adversarial zero-sum games, including partial observation.

paragraphs: Collaborative inference lets users send an encoded version of sensitive data to a service that runs a machine-learning model. Existing approaches assess the privacy of these encodings through attempts to reconstruct the original data. This paper develops a framework for attaching formal privacy guarantees to a neural network after it has been trained.

The key connection is between a network’s local Lipschitz constant and its local sensitivity. These quantities describe how much its output can change near a particular input. The authors extend Propose-Test-Release so that local sensitivity can be used tractably for neural-network queries, turning a mathematical account of local behavior into a mechanism for privacy guarantees.

The framework accommodates arbitrarily trained networks, making its post-training role central to the contribution. Experiments on real-world datasets evaluate its effectiveness, and the paper investigates how adversarial representation learning improves the balance between privacy and utility. The stated result is a formal framework for collaborative inference, alongside evidence about how learned representations can help preserve useful information under privacy protection.
neurips-2023-posthoc-privacy-guarantees-.tldr: A modified Propose-Test-Release framework uses neural-network local sensitivity to provide post-training privacy guarantees for collaborative inference.

paragraphs: Sharpness-Aware Minimization takes a descent step using a gradient evaluated at a perturbed version of the current parameters. Practical implementations normalize the perturbation direction and keep its size constant. Earlier convergence studies often changed one or both choices, leaving uncertainty about whether their conclusions described the optimizer actually used.

This paper analyzes deterministic and stochastic SAM with those practical choices retained. For smooth strongly convex objectives, deterministic SAM has tight global convergence rates of approximately one over the square of the iteration count, up to logarithmic factors. Stochastic SAM instead has an unavoidable additive term of order rho squared, allowing a residual neighborhood around an optimum.

Such residual terms appear for stochastic SAM in every setting considered and for deterministic SAM in the nonconvex cases studied. The authors supply examples showing that the terms cannot simply be removed from the analysis. The conclusions therefore depend on both the objective setting and optimizer variant, demonstrating why convergence intuition from modified versions of SAM may fail to transfer.
neurips-2023-practical-sharpness-aware-m.tldr: Practical SAM has unavoidable residual convergence terms in several analyzed settings, although deterministic SAM can converge globally on smooth strongly convex objectives.

paragraphs: Developing AI for minimally invasive and robot-assisted surgery is constrained by the difficulty of collecting and curating medical data. Ethical considerations also complicate training and testing in clinical environments. SARAMIS addresses this bottleneck by providing anatomical assets that researchers can use to create simulated visual data.

The authors derive 3D meshes, tetrahedral volumes, textures, and diffuse maps from existing open-source CT datasets. The collection covers more than 104 anatomical targets and focuses on human abdominal anatomy. They describe it as the largest open-source collection of rendering assets for these surgical simulation tasks, expanding the available supply of 3D meshes by three orders of magnitude.

GPU-enabled rendering environments accompany the assets so researchers can generate datasets for relevant vision tasks. The paper demonstrates an autonomous colonoscopy-navigation example using assets derived from abdomen-pelvis CT scans. This establishes an example use of the simulation resource; the central contribution is the reusable anatomical collection and rendering infrastructure. The assets are publicly released under a CC-BY-NC-SA license.
neurips-2023-saramis-simulation-assets-f.tldr: SARAMIS supplies a large collection of CT-derived anatomical assets and GPU rendering environments for simulating surgical vision tasks.

paragraphs: Referring video object segmentation identifies the object described by text and outlines it throughout a video. Methods that process each frame separately can struggle to use relationships between frames or interpret descriptions involving changes over time. SOC addresses this problem by organizing visual and textual information at the video level.

The method groups frame-level object representations and associates them with language tokens. This creates a shared representation across both modalities and time steps, allowing the text to guide unified temporal modeling. Multimodal contrastive supervision further encourages the visual and linguistic representations to align across the video, supporting a more coherent understanding of the described object.

The authors report outperforming state-of-the-art competitors on all benchmarks they evaluated. They also find that emphasizing temporal coherence improves segmentation stability and handling of expressions that describe temporal variation. The contribution is therefore a way to connect object evidence across frames with the meaning of the full description, with reported benefits for both benchmark performance and consistency over time.
neurips-2023-soc-semantic-assisted-objec.tldr: SOC aligns language with object representations across an entire video to improve referring-object segmentation and temporal consistency.

paragraphs: Sorting can be expensive when exact comparisons between items are slow. This paper investigates whether imperfect predictions can reduce the number of those comparisons. It studies two sources of help: a predicted sorted position for each item, and a fast but potentially inaccurate comparison procedure available alongside a slower exact one.

For both settings, the authors design simple algorithms whose exact-comparison cost depends on suitably defined errors for individual elements. The bound sums logarithms of those errors. As predictions worsen, the required number of exact comparisons transitions smoothly from linear in the number of items to the familiar n log n scale.

The authors prove that these comparison bounds are optimal for the error measures they examine. This gives a precise account of how prediction quality can translate into savings without requiring predictions to be perfect. Experiments against existing adaptive and nonadaptive sorting algorithms demonstrate practical potential. The result concerns exact-comparison efficiency, tying the value of predictive information to a measurable part of the sorting workload.
neurips-2023-sorting-with-predictions-fb.tldr: Prediction-assisted sorting algorithms use fewer exact comparisons when predictions are good and degrade smoothly as prediction errors grow.

paragraphs: Strategic classification studies people or agents who alter their features to obtain a favorable prediction. This paper considers a realistic complication: different agents have different manipulation abilities, and the learner does not know those abilities. The analysis asks how these personalized, unknown changes affect learning mistakes and the number of examples needed.

The authors formalize an interaction in which a learner deploys a classifier and an agent changes its features within an allowed set. They examine several information patterns, including whether the learner sees original features before or after deployment, manipulated features, or neither. For manipulations bounded by a ball, they establish online mistake bounds and PAC sample-complexity results under these scenarios.

They also investigate more general manipulation sets. In the non-ball setting studied, both mistake bounds and sample complexity have lower bounds proportional to the size of the known hypothesis class, even when original and manipulated features are revealed. This shows how the structure of permitted changes can create substantial learning difficulty despite access to both feature versions.
neurips-2023-strategic-classification-un.tldr: The paper characterizes learning difficulty when agents have unknown, personalized manipulation abilities and the learner receives varying amounts of feature information.

paragraphs: Concept negation aims to keep specified concepts out of generated images through natural-language instructions. The paper identifies a difficulty with existing methods that combine diffusion score or noise predictions: they handle independent concepts but fail to account for relationships between concepts. Excluding a broad category can require recognizing its connection to a specifically named subject.

ProtoRe addresses this issue during generation by identifying unwanted concepts and removing their influence in feature space. It uses CLIP’s language-contrastive knowledge to identify a prototype of a negative concept. That prototype guides the extraction of negative features from outputs, and retrieving these features helps refine the model’s attention maps.

This approach makes concept negation depend on the unwanted concept’s representation and connections, improving flexibility beyond independent exclusions. Across multiple benchmarks and settings, the authors report better purification effectiveness and image fidelity than state-of-the-art methods. The findings support the proposed test-time mechanism as a way to improve generative refusals while retaining the quality of the resulting images.
neurips-2023-towards-test-time-refusals-.tldr: ProtoRe uses CLIP-derived concept prototypes and feature-space purification to improve test-time exclusion of interconnected concepts from generated images.

paragraphs: Adversarial robustness is often studied by bounding how much an attacker can change each individual input. This paper broadens that perspective using Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization. Its threat models allow nonuniform changes across inputs, connecting adversarial attacks with uncertainty about the data distribution and performance on unseen data.

The authors develop a first-order attack algorithm and a multistep version for evaluating these distributional threats. Their algorithms contain FGSM and PGD as special cases, placing familiar pointwise attacks within a wider framework. They also derive a fast asymptotic estimate of adversarial accuracy that is accurate to first order and provides insight even for conventional pointwise attacks.

The resulting bound also yields out-of-sample performance guarantees. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using networks from RobustBench, illustrate the theoretical results. The contribution combines a broader definition of attacker capability with computational tools for examining it, while the accuracy estimate retains its stated asymptotic and first-order character rather than being presented as an exact evaluation.
neurips-2023-wasserstein-distributional-.tldr: Wasserstein distributional threat models generalize pointwise adversarial attacks and support new attack algorithms, accuracy estimates, and out-of-sample guarantees.
